concerns.text: The spec has NO Functional Requirements section and no FR-NNN items. All three user stories (US-01, US-02, US-03) are therefore unbacked by any functional requirement — silent under-specification. Each story's acceptance criteria must be lifted into explicit FR-NNN entries anchored to their story (e.g. FR-001 cosine-distance drift scoring serving US-01).

The spec has NO Success Criteria section and no SC-NNN items. The 'Success Metrics' bullet list at the bottom restates story-level thresholds but is not a SC list with traceability. Every story needs at least one SC-NNN; e.g. US-01 needs an SC for 'p < 0.05 and Cohen's d >= 0.5 separation', US-02 for 'Cohen's Kappa >= 0.6', US-03 for 'Drift AUC within 0.10 of Flan-T5 baseline'.

Stated goal 'Maximum RAM: GB (GitHub Actions free-tier)' has a missing numeric value and no FR/SC backing it, while Constitution Principle VII mandates 7GB/6-hour constraints. Add an FR (and SC) anchoring resource limits to a story or explicitly to the constitution, with the actual number.

Pipeline steps 1-7 describe functionality but carry no story anchors or FR references, so traceability from pipeline to stories cannot be verified. Annotate each step with the story/FR it serves (e.g. 'Step 6: Baseline Comparison (US-03)').

US-01 AC3 requires 'significant separation between benign and novel logs (p < 0.05, Cohen's d ≥ 0.5)', but 'benign' and 'novel' labels can only come from the human annotation workflow defined in US-02. The spec presents US-01 as a self-contained scoring story with no stated dependency on US-02, creating an internal dependency contradiction: US-01's acceptance criteria cannot be evaluated without US-02's outputs. State the dependency explicitly or redefine AC3's reference labels.

'Maximum RAM: GB (GitHub Actions free-tier)' — the numeric value is missing, while the project constitution (Principle VII) specifies 7GB. This is internally incomplete and inconsistent with the constitution's stated constraint; fill in the value.

'Maximum runtime: a bounded duration suitable for benchmark tasks' is vague and inconsistent in precision with the rest of the spec (constitution Principle VII names a 6-hour CPU limit). Use the concrete bound so the constraint is unambiguous.

US-01 AC2 and the Data Model both reference 'the threshold' for review_flag, but no value or selection rule for the threshold is defined anywhere in the spec, while other acceptance criteria (p-values, Kappa, AUC margin) all carry concrete values. Define the threshold or its derivation rule for internal completeness.

'Logs with drift scores above a threshold are flagged' — the threshold value or a deterministic selection procedure (e.g., quantile, validation-set-tuned cutoff) is never stated. An implementer cannot know when review_flag is true; the criterion is unverifiable as written.

'Significant separation between benign and novel logs' does not state the source of the benign/novel labels. Per Constitution VI these must come from the human-annotated gold standard; if bins are formed by sorting on drift score itself, the test is tautological (it only confirms the score has variance). Specify the independent label source and the test (e.g., Mann-Whitney U of drift score vs human novelty label).

'Stratifies logs into high/low drift bins' gives no quantile thresholds. The idea doc says top/bottom 20%; the spec must state the concrete binning rule for deterministic, reproducible execution (Constitution I).

'Logistic regression and Mann-Whitney U tests validate drift score correlation with human labels' — no pass/fail criterion is stated (which statistic, which threshold, one-sided or two-sided). Prior review flagged conflation of logistic regression with Kappa; as written AC5 has no measurable success condition.

'Maximum RAM: GB' is missing its numeric value, and 'a bounded duration suitable for benchmark tasks' is not measurable. State the concrete limits (e.g., 7GB RAM, 6-hour CPU) so the runtime budget can actually be measured per Constitution VII.

'Flagged as a computationally efficient alternative' — the flagging rule is stated (AUC within 0.10) but the inference-time comparison (AC4) has no comparison criterion or reporting format; state what is measured (per-log latency, total wall time) and where it is reported.

Under-reach: the idea's 'Novel Log Collection' step (scrape 500+ post-2025 agent interaction logs from GitHub issues / arXiv agent repos to ensure exposure to novel attack patterns absent from AgentDoG training data) is entirely absent from the spec. The pipeline's 'Data Loading' only fetches 'AgentDoG taxonomy and validation datasets' — no FR or story covers acquiring the novel-log corpus that the research question ('novel, emergent attack vectors') depends on.

US-01 AC3 requires 'significant separation between benign and novel logs (p < 0.05, Cohen's d ≥ 0.5)', but the spec never defines where 'novel' vs 'benign' ground-truth labels come from at the US-01 stage (human labels only arrive in US-02). Without a labeled novel/benign source, AC3 is untestable as scoped and quietly redefines the idea's validation (chi-squared on human 'novel attack' labels across drift bins) into an unspecified separation test.

Under-reach vs idea: the idea specifies 3 annotators labeling each log as 'novel attack'/'known attack'/'benign' and stratifying into top-20%/bottom-20% drift bins, plus a chi-squared test of novel-label distribution across bins. The spec's US-02 omits annotator count, the three-way label scheme, the 20% stratification quantiles, and the chi-squared test (replaced by logistic regression + Mann-Whitney without justification).

The idea pins the embedding model all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (CPU-friendly, constitution VII grounds this choice); the spec never names the embedding model used for centroids or log embeddings. Specify it (or an equivalent CPU-tractable model) for scope fidelity and reproducibility.

'Maximum RAM: GB' is missing the numeric value (idea/constitution: 7GB) and 'a bounded duration' is vague vs the idea's explicit 6-hour CPU limit. Constitution VII makes these concrete bounds; the spec should state them.

'Statistical validation shows significant separation between benign and novel logs (p < 0.05, Cohen's d ≥ 0.5)' — the spec never defines where the 'benign' and 'novel' labels come from for this test. If they are derived from the drift score itself (e.g., high/low drift bins), the test is tautological: comparing a variable across its own quantiles always yields separation. The only independent label source in the spec is US-02's human annotation, but US-01 is presented as independently testable. US-01's validation must be explicitly gated on the human-annotated gold standard (Constitution VI), or the label source must be named and shown independent of the centroid construction.

'Logistic regression and Mann-Whitney U tests validate drift score correlation with human labels' — the comparison groups for the Mann-Whitney U test are unspecified. If the test compares drift scores between the high-drift and low-drift bins (AC1's stratification, which is defined BY the drift score), it is circular and cannot fail. The test must compare drift-score distributions across HUMAN-LABELED groups (novel vs benign), with the human label as the independent grouping variable. Also, logistic regression 'validates correlation' only in the sense of fitting an association; the spec should state the reported statistic (e.g., coefficient significance or AUC), not 'correlation'.

AUC-ROC for both methods requires a ground-truth label, which the spec does not name. If the labels are the taxonomy categories used to build the centroids, the drift method is a nearest-centroid classifier evaluated on its own training labels — a circular validation that cannot support the 'novel threat detection' claim. Additionally, treating Flan-T5's AUC as the reference ('within 0.10') assumes the baseline is accurate on novel patterns; the spec must require the baseline's accuracy to be measured against the human gold standard first, or the comparison is against an unvalidated anchor.

The 'novel' ground truth is never defined as independent of the taxonomy. If human annotators label a log 'novel' partly by reference to the four AgentDoG categories (Safety/Privacy/Bias/Jailbreak), and centroids are means of those same categories, the validation partially restates the construction. The spec must define 'novel attack' operationally (e.g., harmful per annotator judgment but not assignable to any of the four categories by an independent rubric applied without seeing the drift score) and require annotators be blinded to drift scores (blinding of batches is mentioned, but not blinding to the drift bin of each log — stratified batches could leak drift information).

Stratification into 'high/low drift bins' is unspecified (quantile thresholds, inclusion of the middle mass). Prior review flagged 10% vs 20% inconsistency; the spec must pin the thresholds and justify them, since bin choice directly conditions which logs reach human annotation and thus the validation set — an arbitrary choice can bias the estimated drift-label association.

Centroid construction is underspecified: what text constitutes each category's centroid (taxonomy definitions only? labeled example logs? how many?), and with which embedding model? The idea sketch says all-MiniLM-L6-v2, but the spec omits it. Centroid composition materially determines the drift score's meaning; without it the measurement is not reproducible (Constitution I) and its validity cannot be assessed.

Under-reach vs idea: the idea specifies 3 annotators labeling each log as 'novel attack'/'known attack'/'benign' and stratifying into top-20%/bottom-20% drift bins, plus a chi-squared test of novel-label distribution across bins. The spec's US-02 omits annotator count, the three-way label scheme, the 20% stratification quantiles, and the chi-squared test (replaced by logistic regression + Mann-Whitney without justification).

new_concerns.text: FR-005 still uses the placeholder '[deferred]' for the high‑drift and low‑drift quantile thresholds. A concrete quantile (e.g., top 10 % / bottom 10 %) must be specified to make the functional requirement implementable and reproducible.

SC-001 lists FR‑009 (logistic regression) as part of US‑01 success criteria, but FR‑009 belongs to US‑02. This mis‑alignment creates an internal inconsistency between success criteria and the user stories they reference.

Acceptance criterion still uses placeholder '[deferred]' for the high‑drift and low‑drift bin definitions. Replace with the concrete quantile thresholds (e.g., top 10 % and bottom 10 %) so the criterion is directly measurable without relying on FR‑005.

Stratification thresholds remain placeholders ('top [deferred]' and 'bottom [deferred]') in FR-005 and US-02 AC1. The specification must concretely define the quantile cutoffs (e.g., top 10% and bottom 10%) and provide a brief justification, as the current vagueness prevents reproducible and unbiased validation of the drift score.
